author: ribeye
dek: Anthropic's record $81.3 billion IPO soared 17% on its first day of trading — unless you bought it at the open, in which case it fell all afternoon. One Piqua household learned the difference the expensive way.
disclaimer: Parody: the Harlan family of Piqua is fictional. The Anthropic IPO, its share price, and the market sell-off are real, as reported by AFP on Nov. 20, 2026.
headline: Piqua Dad Buys Anthropic at the Open, Watches $111.50 Become $97 Before Dinner

ohio_story: PIQUA, Ohio — Tom Harlan had been waiting for this day for weeks. Harlan, who works the day shift at the propeller plant, had read all about Anthropic, the artificial intelligence company behind the Claude chatbot, and its record-breaking stock market debut. On Thursday morning, just before noon, he did what any man with a brokerage app and a dream would do: he bought ten shares the moment trading opened, at $111.50 apiece. "The man on television said it was the biggest IPO in history," Harlan said, staring at his phone over a bowl of cereal. "I figured if it was the biggest, it could only go up."

By the time Harlan got home from the plant that evening, his ten shares were worth $97.17 each, and the rest of the stock market had not done him any favors either: the Nasdaq and the S&P 500 both fell more than 2% on the same day, which meant his 401(k) had also taken a hit. His wife, Dana, found him at the kitchen table refreshing the price on his phone while the Thanksgiving grocery list sat untouched beside a half-peeled potato. "He has checked the price fourteen times since Thursday," Dana said. "I told him the turkey is not going to brine itself, and neither is the retirement account going to fix itself by staring at it."

Harlan, to his credit, is keeping things in perspective. The shares did close 17% above the $83 price the company set the night before, which means the people who bought them before the opening bell did just fine — it is only the people who bought them at the opening bell who are underwater. "I am now the proud owner of the biggest IPO in history, minus a hundred and forty-five dollars," Harlan said, doing the math out loud for the third time. "The way I see it, I paid $145 to learn what an IPO is. The turkey, at least, I already know how to cook."
real_summary: Anthropic, the artificial intelligence company behind the Claude chatbot, closed 17% higher in its record Nasdaq debut on Thursday, Nov. 19, 2026, defying a broad Wall Street sell-off. The shares were priced at $83 on Wednesday, opened at $111.50 — briefly valuing the company at about $2 trillion — and ended the day at around $97, valuing Anthropic at about $1.75 trillion.

The offering raised a record $81.3 billion, surpassing the $75 billion Elon Musk's SpaceX raised in its June IPO, making it the largest initial public offering in history. Anthropic, founded in 2021 by former OpenAI employees, is the first of the leading AI model developers to list on Wall Street, trading under the ticker "ANT."

The gain came on a rough day for the broader market, with both the tech-heavy Nasdaq and the S&P 500 closing down more than 2%, as investors questioned whether heavy spending on artificial intelligence will pay off. Anthropic's revenue reached $17 billion in the third quarter, up from $1.4 billion a year earlier, though its massive computing costs remain a major question for investors.
source_note: AFP reporting, Nov. 20, 2026: Anthropic shares closed 17% higher in record Nasdaq debut; priced $83, opened $111.50, closed ~$97; record $81.3B raised, largest IPO ever; Nasdaq and S&P 500 down more than 2% the same day.
